hints.title: Exploiting Initial Ordering
hints.text: Nodes are ordered by absolute value, meaning non-negative values are already sorted relative to each other.

hints.title: Negative Node Property
hints.text: Any negative node has a value smaller than all previously seen positive nodes.

hints.title: Head Re-insertion
hints.text: Unlink negative nodes during traversal and insert them at the front of the list in one pass.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.time: O(N) single pass over linked list
variables: N: number of nodes in list
complexity.notes: Moving negative nodes to the head preserves sorted relative order.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: General merge sort takes O(N log N) time and extra pointer manipulation.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Exploiting the existing absolute-value ordering yields optimal linear time and O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should recognize that reversing the relative order of negatives naturally sorts them.
